If both have teams of dedicated people why do movies seem to release more quickly?
Why do most major video games seem to take 3+ years to finish whereas big budget movies might only take a year to finish?

Let's take one scene: man walks up to a table and solves a rubics cube.

Movie: Get man, table and cube. Setup scene and lighting. Setup camera. Record scene over and over till it's perfect.

Game: Write or obtain engine that supports 3D models, physics of the real world, lighting, collision detection, and scripting to model the inner game of solving the rubics cube. Get someone to model the person, table and rubics cube in as much detail as possible. Get someone to rig and animate the person so it moves smoothly and naturally. Also design and model all possible facial expressions to allow the player to show their emotion. Now model the scene so it can be viewed from any angle and anticipate what a player might do in this scene. Put it all together and start testing and bug fixing. The table vanishes and hair physics goes nuts when the player knocks the cube off the table. Go figure out why and solve the other 100 minor problems in the software.

So how can we compare this to animated movies?

Bruce Kuei from Pixar said in an interview "Pixar movies can take anywhere from 4 years to 7 years! The bulk of the production though, such as animation and lighting, only takes about 6 to 8 months."

However, they aren't animating real world graphics and physics. Also they don't have to spend hours upon hours debugging it.
Movie makers don't need to create the actors, or in the case of Lord of the rings, new Zealand. In games everything must be made.
